- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to revert to lower levels after recent high prices, but true prices often continue trending upward.
- Model lags behind true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in upward trends.
- When true prices spike, model forecasts overshoot the peak and then sharply drop, failing to capture the sustained momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, often missing the depth of the subsequent decline.
- Model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days of the forecast, especially when true prices are rising steadily.
- Model shows a tendency to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp reversals or sudden drops in price.
